deities: Shiva as Arunachaleswarar / Annamalaiyar (Agni lingam, fire element)
festivals: Karthigai Deepam / Maha Deepam (10 days, Nov-Dec, with the Maha Deepam lamp lit atop Arunachala hill)

history.dynasty: Pallava, Chola, Pandya, Hoysala and Vijayanagara kings (built in stages); Nattukottai Nagarathars did later renovations
history.period: Present structure mainly 9th-16th century; inscriptions 849-1582 CE
history.summary: One of the largest Shiva temples in India (about 10 hectares), dedicated to Shiva as Arunachaleswarar, the fire (Agni) sthalam of the Pancha Bhoota Sthalas, with his consort Unnamulai Amman. The 7th-century Tevaram classifies it as a Paadal Petra Sthalam, and the 9th-century saint Manikkavasagar composed the Tiruvempaavai here. The complex has four tall gopurams (the 66-metre eastern tower is among India's tallest temple towers), the Vijayanagara-era thousand-pillared hall, and two temple tanks (Brahma Theertham and Sivaganga Theertham). Legend holds that Shiva appeared here as an infinite pillar of fire before Brahma and Vishnu; the sacred 2,668-ft Arunachala hill behind the temple is worshipped as Shiva himself, and the 14-km Girivalam circumambulation on full-moon nights draws lakhs of pilgrims. Note: counts of praharams and gopurams vary across sources (four vs nine gopurams) - verify.

name: Arunachaleswarar Temple
town_description: District headquarters and major temple town built around the Annamalaiyar Temple at the foot of the 2,668-ft sacred Arunachala hill; famous for the 14-km Girivalam circuit and the Karthigai Deepam festival. Ramana Maharshi's ashram sits at the hill's base.

travel.road: Frequent buses from Chennai, Bengaluru, Vellore, Kanchipuram and Viluppuram; taxis available from Chennai airport

visitor_information.best_time: November-February; Karthigai Deepam (Nov-Dec) is the grandest festival but also the most crowded
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM-12:30 PM and 3:30 PM-9:30 PM daily (the HR&CE listing also shows 5:30 AM-8:00 PM)
